cards.m: Masculine and neuter nouns whose stem ends in k, g, ch or l take -u, never -e.
cards.ex: bank → w banku · pociąg → w pociągu · dach → na dachu · hotel → w hotelu · dziecko → o dziecku

cards.m: Every other hard stem takes -e, and that -e softens the consonant in front of it.
cards.ex: sklep → w sklepie · chleb → w chlebie · las → w lesie · miasto → w mieście

cards.m: Masculine and neuter nouns with a soft stem, or a hardened one (c, cz, dz, dż, rz, sz, ż), take -u.
cards.ex: koń → o koniu · morze → w morzu · gracz → o graczu · lekarz → o lekarzu · Paryż → w Paryżu

cards.m: Feminine nouns take -e after a hard stem, -i after a soft one or l, and -y after a hardened one.
cards.ex: szkoła → w szkole · sól → o soli · kuchnia → w kuchni · praca → w pracy · plaża → na plaży

cards.m: This is the single most common error in the case. After c, cz, dz, dż, rz, sz, ż a feminine noun takes -y.
cards.ex: praca → w pracy · noc → w nocy · ulica → na ulicy · twarz → w twarzy · plaża → na plaży

cards.p: -im or -ym? It is spelling, not grammar
cards.m: Adjectives take one ending, written -im after a soft stem and after k, g, and -ym everywhere else.
cards.ex: tani → tanim · polski → polskim · wysoki → wysokim · dobry → dobrym · nowy → nowym

cards.m: No exceptions, whatever the stem. The plural is -ych or -ich.
cards.ex: nowa → w nowej szkole · duża → w dużej sali · dobra → o dobrej książce

cards.m: Every regular plural takes -ach. Exactly three countries take -ech.
cards.ex: w miastach · w lasach · w kinach — but w Niemczech, we Włoszech, na Węgrzech

cards.m: Learners over-apply the exception. These three take the ordinary -ach.
cards.ex: w Czechach · w Indiach · w Chinach — compare w Niemczech

cards.m: Use we when the next word starts with a consonant cluster that w alone cannot open, especially w + consonant.
cards.ex: we Włoszech · we Francji · we Wrocławiu — but w Warszawie, w Polsce

cards.m: Only w, na, o, po, przy govern the locative. Nothing else does.
cards.ex: w domu · na stole · o tobie · po parku · przy oknie

cards.p: Third person pronouns always take n-
cards.m: Because the locative always has a preposition, on / ona / oni always show n- here.
cards.ex: o nim · o niej · o nich — never *o im

cards.m: Three hard-stem masculine nouns that break the rule and take -u.
cards.ex: w domu · o panu · o synu

cards.m: No preposition, no locative. This is what separates it from every other Polish case.
cards.ex: Correct: Myślę o pracy. Wrong: *Myślę pracę / *Myślę pracą.

cards.m: PWN states it without exception: numerals end in -u (spelled -u, -iu or -gu).
cards.ex: o trzech · o pięciu · o dziesięciu · o dwudziestu · o dwojgu

cards.p: The k → c and g → dz shifts
cards.m: Before the feminine -e, k becomes c and g becomes dz.
cards.ex: Polska → w Polsce · rzeka → w rzece · noga → w nodze · droga → w drodze

cards.m: The only shift learners forget, because ch looks like it should stay.
cards.ex: mucha → w musze · ropucha → o ropusze

cards.m: Before -e, t and d soften to ci and dzi (with an i that is not pronounced separately).
cards.ex: kobieta → o kobiecie · świat → na świecie · ogród → w ogrodzie · ślad → na śladzie

cards.m: Two shifts that change the spelling without changing the sound much.
cards.ex: siostra → o siostrze · biuro → w biurze · stół → na stole · szkoła → w szkole

cards.m: City names and nouns in -ów drop the accent and take a soft w.
cards.ex: Kraków → w Krakowie · Lwów → we Lwowie · Rzeszów → w Rzeszowie

cards.p: -um nouns do not decline in the singular
cards.m: Nouns in -um keep their ending in the locative singular.
cards.ex: w muzeum · w centrum · w liceum — but the plural does change: w muzeach

cards.m: A genuinely irregular form, worth memorising whole.
cards.ex: Mieszkam na wsi. (na, not w)

cards.p: ręka: w ręce and w ręku
cards.m: PWN accepts both. Neither is an error.
cards.ex: Trzymam to w ręce. / Trzymam to w ręku.

cards.p: dzień → dniu, but we dnie i w nocy
cards.m: The ordinary form is w dniu. The fixed phrase keeps the older dnie.
cards.ex: w dniu · we dnie i w nocy (obligatory in the phrase)

cards.m: Forms like *tamtem and *dobrem are wrong. The locative adjective ends in -im or -ym.
cards.ex: Correct: o tamtym, o dobrym. Wrong: *o tamtem, *o dobrem.

cards.m: The one real home of the -em ending: geographical names used as nouns.
cards.ex: w Kieleckiem · w Lubelskiem · w Poznańskiem

cards.p: dziecko → dzieciach, oko → oczach, ucho → uszach
cards.m: Three neuter nouns with irregular plural stems. The singular is regular.
cards.ex: o dziecku / o dzieciach · w oku / w oczach · w uchu / w uszach

cards.m: The stem looks irregular, but the plural ending is the ordinary -ach.
cards.ex: o ludziach

cards.m: One of the -ę neuter nouns that swap the stem between numbers.
cards.ex: w imieniu (also = on behalf of) · o imionach

cards.m: The -ę neuters take a -t- stem in the plural.
cards.ex: o zwierzęciu · o zwierzętach

cards.m: The spelling of the feminine -i depends on what stands before the j.
cards.ex: tradycja → o tradycji · stacja → na stacji; aleja → w alei · knieja → w kniei

cards.m: Feminine nouns in -ia take a double i.
cards.ex: historia → o historii · armia → w armii · geografia → o geografii

cards.p: Ukraine: na and w are both correct
cards.m: The Rada Języka Polskiego accepted both in 2022 and recommends w in official texts.
cards.ex: na Ukrainie / w Ukrainie — both correct

cards.p: w domu, na wsi, na Śląsku
cards.m: The w/na contrast is lexical, not logical. These are the high-frequency ones.
cards.ex: w domu · na wsi · na Śląsku · na Mazurach · na Podhalu · na Kubie · na Węgrzech

cards.p: Place vs movement: pod, nad, przed, za
cards.m: These positional prepositions take the instrumental for a static position and the accusative for movement towards. They never take the locative — that is what keeps the five-preposition rule safe.
cards.ex: Kot śpi pod stołem. (N.) / Kot wbiegł pod stół. (B.) · nad morzem (N.) / nad morze (B.)

cards.m: Time expressions without a preposition are instrumental, not locative. Do not force the locative on them.
cards.ex: wieczorem · latem · zimą · wiosną · jesienią

cards.m: Days of the week take the accusative after w. Months take the locative. This asymmetry is real.
cards.ex: w poniedziałek (B.) — but w styczniu (Ms.)

cards.m: Clock time uses o plus the feminine locative of an ordinal, which is an adjective, not a numeral.
cards.ex: o trzeciej · o piątej · o wpół do szóstej

cards.m: A handful of idiomatic locative phrases that are not about place at all.
cards.ex: przy okazji (on occasion) · o zmroku (at dusk) · po wyjściu (after leaving)

items.en: Read sections 1–4: what the case is, its jobs, and the singular endings.
Say the four endings out loud until they feel like one system: -e, -u, -i, -y.
Run drill set 1 (Which ending?) once. Do not aim for 100% yet.
Read section 7 on sound shifts. Learn the pairs, not the words.
Cover the right-hand column and predict each form before you look.
Run drill set 6 (Type the form) — typing forces the spelling.
Read section 5 on the plural, then the three exceptions in section 6.
Repeat out loud: w Niemczech, we Włoszech, na Węgrzech — and w Czechach, w Indiach, w Chinach.
Run drill set 2 (Plural and the exceptions).
Read section 8. Focus on -ym / -ej / -ych and the n- of the third person.
Run drill set 3 (Adjectives, pronouns, numerals).
Mark ten flashcards as known — only the ones you did not have to think about.
Read section 9, one preposition at a time, and section 10 on verb patterns.
Run drill set 4 (Which preposition?) and set 5 (Place or movement?).
Pick five verbs from the table and write one sentence with each.
Read section 11 on the traps — especially the hardened-stem one.
Run drill set 7 (Translate). Write the sentences by hand first if typing is easy.
Review every mistake from the week using the Review button in each set.
Run the final test (set 8) without looking anything up.
Go through the flashcards you marked as not known, and retire the ones you now know.
Come back in a week and run set 8 again. Spacing is the whole point of the plan.

items.en: Read sections 1–2 and say the rhythm aloud: –em, –ą, –ami.
Say five sentences with a tool: piszę piórem / długopisem / ołówkiem…
Do Drill 1 until you score 15+ out of 16.
Write 10 of your own sentences: one tool, one vehicle, one person, one „z”…
List how you travel: pociągiem, autobusem, samochodem, rowerem…
Say who you do things with: z mamą, z kolegą, z przyjaciółmi… (do Drill 4)
Memorise the -mi list: końmi, dziećmi, ludźmi, braćmi, gośćmi, liśćmi, pieniędzmi, przyjaciółmi, księżmi.
Score 9+ in Drill 2.
Do Drill 3 and notice where narzędnik stops and biernik begins.
Describe your room out loud: nad łóżkiem, pod stołem, przed oknem, za drzwiami, między…
Flashcards: mark 15 verbs as „Umiem”.
Write 10 sentences with interesować się / zajmować się / opiekować się / bawić się.
Take the final test, then review the tips you missed.
Ask and answer out loud: Kim chcesz zostać? — Chcę zostać… (10 professions).
